hints: The population is normal, so $\overline{X}$ is normal with mean 35 and standard deviation $\dfrac{8.1}{\sqrt{140}}$ (not 8.1). Standardise: $z = \dfrac{36 - 35}{8.1 \div \sqrt{140}}$.
You want the upper tail, $\text{P}(Z > z)$. Write it as $1 - \Phi(z)$.
Use the normal distribution function on your calculator (or the table) to find $\Phi(z)$ for your $z$, subtract from 1, and give 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**The distribution of the sample mean**

The population is normal with mean $\mu = 35$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 8.1$. For a sample of size $n = 140$ the sample mean $\overline{X}$ is normal with the same mean but a smaller spread:

$$\overline{X} \sim \text{N}\left(35, \frac{8.1^2}{140}\right)$$

Its standard deviation is $\dfrac{8.1}{\sqrt{140}}$. We divide by $\sqrt{140}$ because it is a mean of 140 values.

**Standardise**

Convert 36 to a $z$-value: subtract the mean, divide by the standard deviation.

$$z = \frac{36 - 35}{8.1 \div \sqrt{140}}$$

Calculator: $\sqrt{140} = 11.8322$, so $8.1 \div 11.8322 = 0.68457$ and

$$z = \frac{1}{0.68457} = 1.461$$

This earns the first M1.

**Choose the correct tail**

We want $\text{P}(\overline{X} > 36)$, the area above $z$. The table or calculator gives the area below, $\Phi(z)$, so

$$\text{P}(\overline{X} > 36) = 1 - \Phi(1.461)$$

This earns the second M1.

**Evaluate**

Normal cdf: $\Phi(1.461) = 0.92799$. So

$$1 - 0.92799 = 0.07201$$

(With the unrounded $z = 1.4608$ you get $0.07204$; both round to $0.0720$.)

hints: First find the standard normal value $z$ with $\Phi(z) = 0.986$: use the inverse normal function on your calculator. Keep at least three decimal places: rounding to 2 significant figures loses the mark.
Standardise with the same distribution as in part **(a)**: $\dfrac{a - 35}{8.1 \div \sqrt{140}} = z$, with the $z$ you just found.
Multiply your $z$ by $\dfrac{8.1}{\sqrt{140}}$ and add 35. Give 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**Turn the probability into a z-value**

We are told $\text{P}(\overline{X} < a) = 0.986$. For the standard normal $Z$, the matching statement is $\text{P}(Z < z) = 0.986$, so

$$z = \Phi^{-1}(0.986)$$

On a calculator (inverse normal, area 0.986, mean 0, standard deviation 1): $z = 2.1973$. The scheme accepts 2.197 to 2.198; we use $2.198$.

**Quick check**

Do not round to 2.2 at this point. The mark scheme gives the B1 only for a value that shows more accuracy than 2.2.

**Standardise and solve for a**

As in part **(a)**, $\overline{X}$ has standard deviation $\dfrac{8.1}{\sqrt{140}} = 0.68457$. Set the standardised value equal to $z$:

$$\frac{a - 35}{8.1 \div \sqrt{140}} = 2.198$$

Multiply both sides by $0.68457$:

$$a - 35 = 2.198 \times 0.68457 = 1.5047$$

Add 35:

$$a = 35 + 1.5047 = 36.5047$$
